aria: Animated recap of the Warriors' 126 to 119 overtime home win over Orlando: Stephen Curry's three-point play with 1:38 left in overtime, quarter-by-quarter scoring, his 41 points, the top scorers, how the Warriors won, and the next game against New Orleans.
notes: Box score from the Warriors' 126–119 overtime home win over the Orlando Magic on Nov 7, 2026, from the full box score on Covers (Yahoo Sports' box score matches Orlando's lines), with game details from the AP (via ABC7 San Francisco and La Nación), Yahoo Sports, NBC Sports Bay Area (via Yahoo), DAZN and Open Court. All 126 Warriors points and all 119 Magic points are accounted for in that box score. Curry's 19 points in the fourth quarter and overtime are 14 in the fourth (NBC Sports Bay Area) plus 5 in overtime (Yahoo Sports, Open Court). The Pelicans' record is from the site's standings after Friday's games; they did not play Saturday. Golden State's Monday opponent is New Orleans per the Warriors coverage on Yahoo Sports and the published schedule (one AP version said Charlotte).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Stephen Curry's three-point play with 1:38 left in overtime (the AP's time): with the Warriors down 118–117, he drove and made a floater through contact, then the free throw, for a 120–118 lead they never gave up (Open Court's account). Wendell Carter Jr. then missed two free throws with 1:15 left that would have tied it. The floater is drawn as a short pull-up in the lane and the contact isn't shown. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

Regulation ended 110–110: Curry's runner with 25.2 seconds left put Golden State up 110–108 and Jamal Cain's putback tied it at the end. The quarter chart shows the four regulation quarters; Golden State won overtime 16–9.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Golden State Warriors or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Curry’s listed 6-foot-2 and 200 pounds (Basketball-Reference), with arms scaled to his reported 6-foot-4 wingspan (Sportskeeda). It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
